topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining how previously learned immune components interact during the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Immune Recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and Pattern Recognition Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbes and cellular damage through conserved molecular patterns and intracellular or surface receptor signaling pathways.

topics.label: Cellular Responses, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cell activation coordinates local leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic drainage, and systemic physiological responses during inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammatory States
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the passive and active mechanisms that shut down inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and manage chronic or persistent immune challenges.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and announces the upcoming session on the complement system.
